deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 47-50): Grothendieck is axiomatizing 'dérivateurs' (a 2-functor D from small categories to categories, with Der 1-5, 5'). On the previous page he tests the axioms on a Mayer-Vietoris situation. A space or category X lies over a two-piece index Psi. It is covered by X_a and X_b with 'intersection' X_0. For xi in D(X) the object gamma = K_* phi_*(xi) in D(Delta^1 x Delta^1) has vertices H_D(X), H_D(X_a), H_D(X_b), H_D(X_0). By construction gamma is cartesian, which is cohomological descent. When X is cofibrant over Psi it 'should' also be cocartesian, which is the full Mayer-Vietoris statement. He suspects this does not follow from Der 1-5, 5', so he adds a provisional axiom Der 6 (cohomological form, using phi_* and K_*).

This page first states a dual, homological variant 'Der 6'' (provisional). Let Q be the corner category a -> 1 <- b. Suppose X is fibred over Q, or equivalent up to a Q-equivalence to a diagram X_a <- X_0 -> X_b in Cat. Then for xi in D(X) cartesian, i.e. 'locally constant' (fibrewise inverse images are isos), the pushforward phi_!(xi) in D(Q) is cocartesian in a restricted sense, and also cartesian. The cocartesianness is read through the cone Q^c, apparently Q with an extra initial vertex 0' mapping to a and b. So Q^c is just the square Delta^1 x Delta^1. This is Mayer-Vietoris for homology with locally constant coefficients.

He then remarks that Der 6' for D does not imply Der 6 for the opposite derivator D°. Passing to opposites exchanges ! and *, fibred and cofibred, cartesian and cocartesian. He sees no way to relate them except in the exceptional case where A = D(e) carries a duality functor exchanging homology and cohomology.

Conclusion: the right axiom, covering both Der 6 and its dual Der 6bis, is self-dual. The new 'Der 6' reads: for gamma in D(Delta^1 x Delta^1), gamma is cartesian iff it is cocartesian. The next page derives consequences: in a bicartesian square, i_1 iso implies i_0 iso, and j_1 iso implies j_0 iso. It also asks that the induced derivators D_I inherit the property, and proves a lemma via the adjunction xi -> p^* p_! xi for p induced by pr_1 : Delta^1 x Delta^1 -> Delta^1.

In modern terms, the page arrives at the stability axiom for derivators: homotopy pullback squares coincide with homotopy pushout squares. It reaches it by symmetrizing a Mayer-Vietoris/descent requirement under the duality D -> D°.
errors: The final self-dual axiom omits pointedness. In the modern definitions (Groth; Lurie, Higher Algebra 1.1.3.4 for infinity-categories) stability is 'pointed + cartesian squares = cocartesian squares'. Whether bicartesian-coincidence alone forces D(e) to be pointed is not addressed. In Grothendieck's intended examples (derived categories of abelian categories, so additive) this is harmless, but as a general axiom it is a gap or at least unexamined.

Der 6' as stated is only a sufficient-condition / special-case formulation. The restricted sense of 'cocartesian' and the hypothesis 'fibred over Q or Q-equivalent to a diagram in Cat' are not made precise on the page. The text is hastily written and partly illegible.
The claim that Der 6' for D does not imply Der 6 for D° is offered as an impression ('je ne vois pas'), not proved.

ideas.what: Provisional axiom Der 6' (homological Mayer-Vietoris): for X fibred over the corner category Q and xi locally constant, phi_!(xi) in D(Q) is both cocartesian (via the cone Q^c) and cartesian.
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy-exactness / Mayer-Vietoris (homotopy pushout) axiom for derivators; descent for homotopy colimits over spans
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Heller (1988) and Cisinski's work on homotopy exact squares; Mayer-Vietoris classically
ideas.where_published: Possibly related material in 'Les Dérivateurs' (1990-91, ed. Künzer/Malgoire/Maltsiniotis); unsure

ideas.what: Observation that the axiom system must be invariant under passing to the opposite derivator D°, and that cohomological and homological versions are exchanged only under a duality functor on D(e).
ideas.modern_name: Duality principle for derivators (D vs D^op)

ideas.what: Self-dual axiom: a square gamma in D(Delta^1 x Delta^1) is cartesian iff cocartesian.
ideas.modern_name: Stable (triangulated) derivator / stable infinity-category axiom (bicartesian squares)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Heller (stable homotopy theories, 1988/1997), Franke (1996), Maltsiniotis (triangulated derivators, 2001/2007), Groth (2013); Lurie for infinity-categories
ideas.where_published: Possibly in Les Dérivateurs (1990-91), unsure; not in Pursuing Stacks to my knowledge

ideas.what: Motivation of the stability axiom from Mayer-Vietoris / cohomological descent for a two-piece cover: the descent square is cartesian by construction and should also be cocartesian.
ideas.modern_name: Mayer-Vietoris squares as bicartesian squares in a stable setting

missed.claim: A dated-early (archive: from 1982, likely c. 1983) formulation by Grothendieck of the stability axiom for derivators: cartesian squares = cocartesian squares in D(Delta^1 x Delta^1). It is reached as the self-dual symmetrization of a Mayer-Vietoris axiom (Der 6) and its dual (Der 6bis). This would predate Heller's 1988 'Homotopy theories' and the Franke/Maltsiniotis triangulated-derivator axioms. The priority record usually starts the stable/triangulated derivator notion later.
missed.quote: "Der 6" Si γ∈D(Δ¹×Δ¹), γ est cartésien ssi il est cocartésien.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is relevant to the history and priority of stable derivators and stable infinity-categories. It also shows that the bicartesian-square characterization of stability arose from descent/Mayer-Vietoris considerations and from the D <-> D° duality, not from triangulated-category octahedra.

missed.claim: Grothendieck states that Der 6' (homological Mayer-Vietoris for locally constant coefficients on fibred objects) does not imply Der 6 for D° except when D(e) carries a homology/cohomology duality. The precise relation between the one-sided Mayer-Vietoris axioms and full stability is left open.
missed.quote: NB Der 6' pour D n'implique pas Der 6 pour D°. Je ne vois pas comment ... en dehors du cas exceptionnel où on a ... une fonctorialité ... et une correspondance par dualité entre cohomologie et homologie.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests studying 'semi-stable' derivators satisfying only one Mayer-Vietoris half, and how this relates to pointedness and to excision axioms, as in Goodwillie calculus and excisive functors. This seems only partially treated in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The final axiom is exactly the modern stability axiom for derivators, written in Grothendieck's hand c. 1983 and derived from a Mayer-Vietoris/duality argument. This is a notable early, unpublished occurrence relevant to priority. However, the notion itself is standard today, Grothendieck's derivator ideas are known to have influenced Maltsiniotis' formulation, and the page contains no new theorem.
transcription_corrections: Title line: '"Der 6'" (provisoire) 14' — the '14' is an old page number. The marginal 'Axiome provisoire' is a scratched-out annotation.

Q^c: in the drawing the extra vertex 0' appears to map to a and b (arrows 0'->a, 0'->b), making Q^c the square Delta^1 x Delta^1. It is not 'a -> 0' <- b' as transcribed (uncertain reading of arrowheads).
'pour i Q-équivalence près' probably reads 'pour une Q-équivalence près'. 'dans Cat' should be the category of categories (written 'Cat'), not script A.
'φ_!(γ)' should likely be 'φ_!(ξ)'. 'est une [?] semblement cocartésien' probably reads 'est non seulement cocartésien (sens restreint), mais aussi cartésien'.
'vu [?] l. c.' probably reads 'i.e. loc. const.' (locally constant), consistent with 'cartésien'.
'il semblerait que les [...] englobe Der 6 et Der 6bis bien i...' probably reads 'il semblerait que l'axiome englobant Der 6 et Der 6bis bien à la fois soit le suivant!'.
Left margin bottom reads roughly 'La dualité ...' and '"L'axiome magique"' (uncertain).
